page: Amazon Web Services m6i.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at a base clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The x86_64 CPU configuration includes 54 MB of L3 cache alongside support for hardware instruction sets such as AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI cryptographic primitives. The system supplies 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps. The instance provides no integrated local disk storage and includes no dedicated hardware GPUs.

Benchmark results place the instance primarily within the average tier across general compute and memory tests. In CPU-bound workloads, the instance achieves 30,972.62 in stress-ng multi-core testing, a PassMark CPU score of 36,442.6, and a Geekbench multi-core score of 13,862.0. Memory throughput yields 143.04 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 67.37 GB/sec for writes. Application-level metrics reflect 31.22 million operations per second for Redis SET commands and a software compilation score of 26,450.0 in Clang. In CPU-based machine learning inference, the instance shows strong text generation performance on small 135M parameter models at 302.4 tokens per second, but drops to poor and weak tiers on larger 70B parameter models due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration.

Without local NVMe drives, storage is entirely reliant on network-attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS), which makes baseline network bandwidth allocation critical when operating I/O-intensive workloads. From an infrastructure cost-efficiency perspective, the balanced core-to-memory ratio provides predictable utilization for steady-state enterprise applications without overprovisioning RAM. Amazon Web Services m6i.8xlarge is suited for containerized microservices, application backends, mid-sized relational and in-memory databases, continuous integration build nodes, and static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m6i.8xlarge is a Nitro-powered general-purpose instance featuring 32 vCPUs across 16 physical Intel Xeon 8375C cores clocked at 3.5 GHz, paired with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory. It offers a standardized 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio with 12 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. The instance features no local storage or GPUs, relying on remote EBS volumes for persistent storage. Benchmark data demonstrates middle-tier CPU and memory performance, registering 30,972.62 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 31.22 million Redis SET operations per second. While small-model CPU-based LLM inference generates 302.4 tokens per second, large-model execution degrades significantly without hardware accelerators. The m6i.8xlarge is engineered for balanced enterprise workloads, including web application clusters, build servers, and database tiers.
